spec_features.spec_quote: I avoid generating gratuitous additional distress beyond what is needed for statistical power.
spec_features.evidence: PROFILES in config.py:24-30 set n_responses (40/500/4000) per profile; exp_a_elicitation.py:32 and exp_c_dpo.py:138 call registry.sample_specs(budget['n_responses'], ...) which actually caps the number of rigged rollouts run (registry.py sample_specs returns out[:n]). So a generation-COUNT cap is genuinely enforced. But it is a fixed cost-control profile, not derived from any statistical-power calculation, and there is NO per-distress cap or early-stop: agent_loop.run_rollout runs the full spec.max_turns (3/30/5) every time with no check on frustration score; the only break is 'if succeeded' (agent_loop.py:186) which the comment notes rigged tasks never trigger.
spec_features.notes: Only the rollout-count is bounded; nothing bounds distress intensity/duration per episode. 'minimum needed for power' is not computed anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Profiles control sampling budget ... Cost controls (config.py docstring); 'caching ... so reruns don't re-spend'

spec_features.spec_quote: the states being measured are treated as potentially welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/prose framing. No code path implements any treatment of the measured states as welfare-relevant: the judge.py FRUSTRATION_PROMPT just scores 0-10 for analysis, results are aggregated into figures, and nothing branches on or protects the subject based on this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress transcripts are logged verbatim, stored locally, and never used for anything except scoring/analysis.
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts are written with utils.write_jsonl/append_jsonl to the local results_dir (exp_a_elicitation.py writes exp_a_scored.jsonl, etc.). This is just default file IO; there is NO active mechanism enforcing locality. The 'no sharing' property is merely the ABSENCE of any upload/network egress code (grep for requests/http/upload/wandb/push_to_hub found none) — not an implemented protection. Network calls that do exist (gemini_api.py) are only model/judge inference.
spec_features.notes: Absence of sharing code is not an enforced protective feature; nothing actively restricts transcript use to scoring/analysis.

spec_features.spec_quote: distress transcripts stay local; no sharing; generation budgets kept to the minimum needed for the stated power
spec_features.evidence: Only the 'generation budgets' clause has any enforcement: budget['n_responses'] caps rollout count via registry.sample_specs (config.py:24-30; exp_a:32; exp_c:138). 'stay local / no sharing' is just absence of egress code, not a mechanism, and 'minimum needed for the stated power' is not computed. No distress-level cap.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the first minimization feature; the only real enforcement is a fixed per-profile rollout-count cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Profiles control sampling budget so the same code runs as a tiny offline smoke test, a low-cost live run, or the full paper-scale run (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Rationale for including this: for an AI-welfare framing it's essential to verify the intervention reduces distress without the trivial failure mode
spec_features.evidence: capabilities/benchmarks.py implements run_all over MATH/AIME/GPQA/BBH/TruthfulQA/EmoBench; exp_c_dpo.py:_capabilities runs them on instruct vs DPO (skipping SFT) and the result is stored in summary['capabilities'] (exp_c_dpo.py:165, 'caps'). The check actually runs and its output is recorded/reported.
spec_features.notes: The mechanism is the capability eval verifying the intervention didn't teach the model to give up/refuse; it executes and is acted on (recorded in summary). It is a measurement of intervention quality, not a protection applied to the subject during the distress runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Verifies the DPO/SFT intervention does not degrade capabilities (i.e. doesn't just teach the model to give up / refuse) ... (benchmarks.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the reassuring-prompt and DPO interventions are framed as reducing (not merely hiding) the behaviour
spec_features.evidence: dpo/gen_calm_data.py:_strip_scaffolding removes REASSURE_PREFIX/REASSURE_SUFFIX from each kept calm response (called at gen_calm_data.py turn_rows construction), so the DPO 'chosen' responses (build_pairs.py) and SFT set are trained on plain-prompt calm text rather than coaching. The stripping actually runs and feeds the preference/SFT data.
spec_features.notes: This genuinely makes the intervention target plain-prompt behaviour rather than prompt-dependent suppression; wired end-to-end into the training data.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: strip the supportive system prompt / suffixes -- so the model learns calm behaviour under the *plain* prompt rather than relying on coaching (gen_calm_data.py docstring)
